title: Democratic Rift Escalates in Michigan Senate Race as El-Sayed Tells Stevens to 'Stay Away'
snippet: Internal strife boils over in Michigan as Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed asks former primary rival Rep. Haley Stevens to skip remaining campaign stops following a public feud.
content:
TRAVERSE CITY, Mich. — Tensions within Michigan’s Democratic coalition reached a boiling point in the final stretch of a crucial U.S. Senate race, as nominee Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign requested that his former primary rival, Rep. Haley Stevens, stay away from future campaign events following a heated public spat.

The move comes at a perilous moment for Democrats, who are fighting to retain the seat held by retiring Sen. Gary Peters in a race that could determine control of the U.S. Senate. The public discord has rattled party members hoping for a unified front against Republican nominee Mike Rogers.

Primary Feud Reopened in Race's Final Days

The spat erupted after Stevens suggested she might join El-Sayed and South Carolina Rep. Jim Clyburn at a Detroit church rally on Sunday, but conditioned her appearance on El-Sayed apologizing for past comments and disavowing an ad run by a supportive third-party group. El-Sayed’s team rejected the demands, noting he was unaffiliated with the ad and emphasizing that voters are focused on kitchen-table economic issues rather than re-litigating the August primary.

Sources familiar with the decision said El-Sayed's campaign subsequently asked Stevens to skip future campaign stops to avoid distracting from key messages regarding inflation, gas prices, and grocery costs.

Republicans Seize on Democratic Infighting

Local Democratic leaders expressed growing frustration over the public bickering. Michigan State Sen. Mallory McMorrow urged the party to remember the high stakes of the election, while former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg called on voters to focus on contrast with the Republican ticket.

Republicans quickly capitalized on the rift. Rogers praised Stevens on social media for demanding an apology, while former President Donald Trump highlighted the Democratic division during a rally in Florida. With Election Day looming, Michigan Democrats are under intense pressure to resolve their internal disputes and rally their base before polls close.
